## Tutorials

The CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() function returns the current date and time.

Note:The date and time is returned as "YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS" 
(string) or as YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.uuuuuu (numeric).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP();

---

CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()

---

SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() + 1;
```

## Tutorials

The CURTIME() function returns the current time.

Note:The time is returned as 
"HH-MM-SS" (string) or as HHMMSS.uuuuuu (numeric).

Note:This function equals theCURRENT_TIME()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CURTIME();

---

CURTIME()

---

SELECT CURTIME() + 1;
```

## Tutorials

The DATE() function extracts the date part from a datetime 
expression.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DATE("2017-06-15");

---

DATE(
expression
)

---

SELECT DATE("2017-06-15 09:34:21");

---

SELECT DATE("The 
  date is 2017-06-15");

---

SELECT DATE(OrderDate) FROM Orders;
```

## Tutorials

The DATEDIFF() function returns the number of days between two date values.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DATEDIFF("2017-06-25", "2017-06-15");

---

DATEDIFF(
date1
,
date2
)

---

SELECT DATEDIFF("2017-06-25 09:34:21", "2017-06-15 15:25:35");

---

SELECT DATEDIFF("2017-01-01", 
  "2016-12-24");
```

## Tutorials

The DATE_ADD() function adds a time/date interval to a date and then returns the date.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DATE_ADD("2017-06-15", INTERVAL 10 DAY);

---

DATE_ADD(
date
, INTERVAL
value addunit
)

---

SELECT DATE_ADD("2017-06-15 09:34:21", INTERVAL 15 MINUTE);

---

SELECT DATE_ADD("2017-06-15 09:34:21", INTERVAL -3 HOUR);

---

SELECT DATE_ADD("2017-06-15", INTERVAL -2 MONTH);
```
